verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego' on April 10, 2026 at 8:07 p.m. ET; R2: 'splashdown around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10, off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)' off the coast of San Diego.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact location, date, and time (converting ET to PDT).

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; also 'roughly 40-50 miles southwest of San Diego'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to the precise distance and location in R1.

verifications.claim: The crew was recovered by U.S. Navy personnel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Navy divers', 'U.S. Navy MH-60 Seahawk', 'Navy chopper'; R4: 'U.S. Navy helicopters'; R2: 'Recovery teams will retrieve the crew using helicopters'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe U.S. Navy involvement in crew extraction and transport.

verifications.claim: The landing location was the Pacific Ocean, southwest of San Diego, CA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly 40-50 miles southwest of San Diego'; R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of southwest Pacific Ocean location relative to San Diego.

verifications.claim: The recovery ship was U.S.S. John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'USS John P. Murtha'; R2: 'USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'USS John P Murtha'; R4: 'USS John P. Murtha'.
verifications.reasoning: Consistently named across multiple sources as the recovery ship.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission duration was 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day trip'; R3: '10-day mission'; R4: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R5: '10-day mission'; R8: '10-day mission'.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state 10-day mission duration; R3 notes officially recorded as 10 days despite precise timing.

verifications.claim: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman ... Christina Koch and Victor Glover ... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and ... Jeremy Hansen'; identical in others.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed consistently across sources.

verifications.claim: The crew returned from a lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'after their historic 10-day trip to the moon'; R3: 'flyby of the Moon'; R5: 'flyby around the moon'; R4: 'around the Moon and back'.
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe the mission as a lunar flyby without landing.

verifications.claim: The crew and capsule were recovered for return to base
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crew will be extracted ... flown to USS John P. Murtha ... Orion will then be returned to Naval Base San Diego, before being transported back to the Kennedy Space Center'; R4: 'crew ... flown to the USS John P. Murtha ... return Orion to U.S. Naval Base San Diego before returning it to NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail recovery of both crew (to Houston) and capsule (to Kennedy Space Center).
